stages.name: Measuring and showing output gaps
stages.title: Measuring and showing output gaps
stages.sub: After this you can explain why output gaps are hard to measure and show one on an AD/AS diagram.

steps.q: A statistician wants to measure the maximum sustainable output of the whole economy right now. Can she go and count it directly, the way she could count last month's actual output?
steps.right: No, it has to be estimated
steps.wrong: Yes, it can be read straight off the records
steps.hint: Actual output gets recorded as things are sold and made. Is the maximum the economy could sustainably produce recorded anywhere?

steps.q: A government body publishes this year's growth figure, then updates it twice over the next two years as more information comes in. Will the very first estimate always turn out to be exactly right?
steps.wrong: Yes, the first figure is final
steps.hint: Think about how statistics offices work: is the first number always the last word?

steps.q: If potential output can only be estimated, and the actual output figures used to compare against it keep changing, how confident can economists be about the true size of an output gap?
steps.right: Not very confident, it is uncertain
steps.wrong: Very confident, the gap is precisely known
steps.hint: Combine the two problems: an estimated benchmark plus a figure that keeps changing.

steps.q: An AD curve shows how much buyers want to spend at each price level. To compare it with what the economy is capable of producing, which side of the economy must the second curve show?
steps.right: The producing side: what firms supply
steps.wrong: The spending side: what buyers demand
steps.hint: You already have the buying side. What is on the other side of the whole economy?

steps.prompt: Drag and drop the 4 key terms in the order they build on each other.

steps.q: On the diagram, suppose the point where AD crosses AS sits to the right of the vertical line marking potential output. Is actual output above or below what the economy can sustainably produce?
steps.hint: Right of the potential output line means more output than the sustainable maximum.
